lines: -- Since Spark 5.0, the Spark Thrift Server refuses to start when `hive.server2.enable.doAs` is `true` and `hive.server2.authentication` verifies user identities (any recognized type other than `NONE`/`NOSASL`). It impersonates the connecting user for Hive metastore calls and driver-side file system access, but executor-side data access still runs as the server's own service identity, so storage-level permissions are checked against the service principal rather than the connecting user (SPARK-5159). Spark 4.4 logs a warning for the same configuration. To restore the previous behavior, set `spark.sql.hive.thriftServer.allowIneffectiveDoAs` to `true`. Setting `hive.server2.enable.doAs` to `false` also starts the server, but note that it stops impersonating metastore calls as well, so it is not a no-op.

+- Since Spark 5.0, the Spark Thrift Server refuses to start when `hive.server2.enable.doAs` is `true` and `hive.server2.authentication` verifies user identities (any recognized type other than `NONE`/`NOSASL`). It impersonates the connecting user for Hive metastore calls and driver-side file system access, but executor-side data access still runs as the server's own service identity, so storage-level permissions are checked against the service principal rather than the connecting user (SPARK-5159). Spark 4.4 and 4.5 log a warning for the same configuration. To restore the previous behavior, set `spark.sql.hive.thriftServer.allowIneffectiveDoAs` to `true`. Setting `hive.server2.enable.doAs` to `false` also starts the server, but note that it stops impersonating metastore calls as well, so it is not a no-op.

- Since Spark 5.0, Spark requires Java 21 or later. Users who ran Spark 4.x on Java 17 can see two differences that come from Java. The datetime pattern letter `F` is the aligned week of month instead of the aligned day of week in month (JDK-8282081). For example, `date_format(date '2019-12-31', 'F')` returns `5` instead of `3`. Converting a `FLOAT` or `DOUBLE` value to a string gives the shortest decimal that represents the value (JDK-4511638). For example, `CAST(CAST(4567890123456789 AS FLOAT) AS STRING)` returns `4.56789E15` instead of `4.5678899E15`. A cast from `FLOAT` or `DOUBLE` to `DECIMAL` goes through this string, so its result can change as well. For example, `CAST(1.0751133388005187E17D AS DECIMAL(38, 0))` returns `107511333880051870` instead of `107511333880051872`.

+- Since Spark 4.5, `LIST FILES`, `LIST JARS` and `LIST ARCHIVES` in a session whose artifacts are isolated list the files, jars and archives added to the session and those added to the `SparkContext` outside of any session, such as with `--files`, `--jars` and `--archives`, but no longer those added by the other sessions, such as with `ADD FILE` or `SparkSession.addArtifact`. Previously, they listed those of every session. Artifacts are isolated by default, and always in the sessions of a Spark Connect server. Spark does not isolate them in `spark-shell`, in PySpark when PySpark creates the `SparkContext`, or in Scala and Java sessions whose builder enables Hive support, such as with `enableHiveSupport()`, so those sessions still list all of them. `SparkContext.listFiles`, `SparkContext.listJars` and `SparkContext.listArchives` are unchanged. To restore the previous behavior, set `spark.sql.legacy.listAllSessionsResources` to `true`.

- Since Spark 4.4, `arrays_zip` accepts array-valued map lookups with computed, `NULL`, or non-string keys. Previously, it tried to use these keys as literal output field names and failed. For example, `SELECT to_json(arrays_zip(map(1, array(10))[1]))` now returns `[{"0":10}]`, where `0` is the first argument's field name. String literal keys also use positional names when collation adds a cast before field naming.

- Since Spark 4.4, a function created by `CREATE FUNCTION ... AS 'class'` whose class implements `org.apache.spark.sql.connector.catalog.functions.UnboundFunction` and extends either a Hive UDF class (such as `UDF` or `GenericUDF`) or `org.apache.spark.sql.expressions.UserDefinedAggregateFunction` runs as a DataSource V2 function instead of a Hive UDF or Spark UDAF, including functions created in earlier versions. Its result type, argument coercion, and null handling are defined by the V2 implementation selected by `UnboundFunction.bind`. Hive's `@UDFType` and Spark UDAF's `deterministic` property do not control the V2 path. For scalar functions, determinism uses `BoundFunction.isDeterministic()` (default `true`) and the arguments' determinism. A call with constant arguments can therefore become eligible for constant folding during query planning instead of being evaluated per row.

- Since Spark 4.4, `next_day` and `last_day` fail with `DATETIME_OVERFLOW` when the result is later than the maximum `DATE`, `+5881580-07-11`, and `trunc` fails with it when the result is earlier than the minimum `DATE`, `-5877641-06-23`, regardless of `spark.sql.ansi.enabled`. Previously, these functions silently returned a wrong date, in most cases one at the other end of the `DATE` range; for example, `last_day(DATE'+5881580-07-11')` returned `-5877641-07-12` and `trunc(DATE'-5877641-06-23', 'MONTH')` returned `+5881580-06-20`, while `trunc` to `QUARTER` failed with `ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW`. `next_day` and `trunc` to `WEEK` also returned a wrong date for the first days of the `DATE` range; for example, `next_day(DATE'-5877641-06-23', 'MO')` and `trunc(DATE'-5877641-07-01', 'WEEK')` returned `-5877641-06-25`, a Thursday, and now return `-5877641-06-29`.

- Since Spark 4.4, a Variant `TIMESTAMP` value is rendered in the session time zone (`spark.sql.session.timeZone`) when it is nested in an array, map, or struct that is cast to `STRING`, in `Dataset.show()`, and in the output of the spark-sql CLI and the Thrift server, as a top-level `CAST(v AS STRING)` already does. Previously, these paths rendered it in UTC. For example, with `spark.sql.session.timeZone` set to `America/Los_Angeles`, `CAST(named_struct('a', CAST(TIMESTAMP'2020-01-01 00:00:00Z' AS VARIANT)) AS STRING)` returns `{"2019-12-31 16:00:00-08:00"}` instead of `{"2020-01-01 00:00:00+00:00"}`. The rendered text carries an explicit offset, so it still denotes the same instant. Sessions in UTC are not affected.
